trace.final_response:
The only valid factory is `createDecorator<T>(serviceId)`.

- Identifiers are cached in `_util.serviceIds`, a `Map` keyed by the service ID string. `createDecorator` returns the existing function on a cache hit; otherwise it creates the callable identifier, assigns its string representation, caches it, and returns it. Thus, repeated calls with the same string have identical token identity. [instantiation.ts:14]({REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r01-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:14) [instantiation.ts:107]({REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r01-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:107)

- The identifier is also a parameter decorator. When invoked with the required `(target, key, index)` shape, it calls `storeServiceDependency`, which records `{ id, index }` on the constructor’s `$di$dependencies` property. `$di$target` marks the constructor that owns that array: dependencies are appended only for the same owner; otherwise a new array is installed, preventing an inherited constructor from mutating its parent’s metadata. `getServiceDependencies` returns that array or `[]`. [instantiation.ts:16]({REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r01-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:16) [instantiation.ts:97]({REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r01-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:97)

- One directly affected importer is `log.ts`: it imports `createDecorator` and uses it to create `ILogService` and `ILoggerService`. Changes to identity caching or decorator metadata recording therefore directly affect these service tokens and their constructor injection. [log.ts:19]({REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r01-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/log/common/log.ts:19)

arguments.query: Find the only valid way to create a ServiceIdentifier; explain identifier caching and how constructor dependencies are recorded; identify a directly affected caller or importer if behavior changes.

arguments.symbol_signature: interface ServiceIdentifier < T >
function storeServiceDependency ( id : ServiceIdentifier < unknown > , target : Function , index : number ) : void
function createDecorator < T > ( serviceId : string ) : ServiceIdentifier < T >

trace.final_response:
The only supported factory is `createDecorator<T>(serviceId)`, explicitly documented as the “only valid way” to create the callable `ServiceIdentifier<T>` interface. [instantiation.ts:91](/{REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r02-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:91) [instantiation.ts:106](/{REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r02-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:106)

Identifiers are interned in `_util.serviceIds`, a `Map` keyed by the service-name string. `createDecorator` returns the existing function object when present; otherwise it creates the parameter decorator, assigns its string representation, caches it, and returns it. Thus repeated calls with the same string preserve object identity. [instantiation.ts:14](/{REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r02-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:14) [instantiation.ts:109](/{REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r02-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:109)

When used as a constructor-parameter decorator, the identifier calls `storeServiceDependency(id, target, index)`. That stores `{id, index}` on the constructor under `$di$dependencies`. The `$di$target` ownership marker ensures an inheriting constructor receives its own array instead of mutating inherited metadata; subsequent dependencies on that same constructor are appended. `getServiceDependencies` returns this array, or `[]`. [instantiation.ts:16](/{REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r02-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:16) [instantiation.ts:97](/{REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r02-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:97)

A directly affected caller is `standaloneServices.initialize`: it recreates an identifier from each override’s string key and immediately uses that object to look up and update `serviceCollection`. The repository-defined only valid factory is `createDecorator<T>(serviceId)`. `ServiceIdentifier<T>` is a callable parameter-decorator interface, and the source explicitly designates `createDecorator` as its sole valid creator. [instantiation.ts:91]({REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r03-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:91) [instantiation.ts:107]({REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r03-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:107)

Identifiers are interned in the module-level `_util.serviceIds: Map<string, ServiceIdentifier<any>>`. `createDecorator` returns the existing function for a previously seen string; otherwise it creates the decorator, gives it a string representation, caches it, and returns it. Thus a service string has canonical function identity, regardless of the generic type supplied by callers. [instantiation.ts:14]({REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r03-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:14) [instantiation.ts:109]({REPO_ROOT}/target/benchmarks/agent-navigation/v040-release-candidate/r03-huge-vscode-v0.4/huge-vscode/src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiation.ts:109)

When used as a constructor-parameter decorator, the identifier requires the three decorator arguments and calls `storeServiceDependency(id, target, index)`. Dependencies are stored on the constructor under `$di$dependencies` as `{ id, index }[]`. `$di$target` marks metadata owned by that constructor; otherwise a fresh array is installed, avoiding mutation of inherited constructor metadata. `getServiceDependencies` returns that array or `[]`.
